transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Simmons (Hillcrest Head of AI), Jorge Ramirez (CTO), Priya Nair (Security), Tom Evans (Dev Lead)

Summary: Quick product walkthrough focused on rate limiting, quotas, and multi-tenant controls (org and project keys) in the Console and API. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated for a multi-tenant patient-facing assistant; main concerns are per-tenant isolation, burst capacity, cost predictability, and auditability.

Topics: rate limits (per-key, per-project), org/project keys, quotas, credit limits, console UI, RBAC & SSO, audit logs, KMS/encryption, pilot plan and benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00:03] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see most folks are here, we'll do a 45-ish minute walkthrough, focus on how rate limits and org/project keys work in Redwood's Console and API, then leave time for Q&A.
[00:00:12] Laura: Sounds great, Maya. Thanks. We're mostly interested in how we can map our tenants to projects and make sure a single tenant can't blow our budget.
[00:00:20] Ravi: Yep totally. Quick intro - I'm Ravi, I'll jump into the Console and demo the org/project keys flow and show the per-route rate limits, token-level billing breakdown, and how to set quotas and alerts.
[00:00:33] Jorge: Quick one, are we recording?
[00:00:34] Maya: Yes recorded, per e-mail. OK Ravi, over to you.
[00:00:38] [00:01:05] Ravi: (screen share) Alright, Console home. First, at the top-level org you can see global usage and then a projects list. For Hillcrest you'd typically create one project per customer tenant or per internal product depending on your model. Each project gets a project API key, which is scoped to that project.
[00:01:25] Tom: So project key = per-tenant key?
[00:01:27] Ravi: Exactly. You can issue multiple keys per project - e.g., mobile key, server key - and each key can have its own rate limit overrides or be attached to routes.
[00:01:38] Laura: Can we do per-route limits? Like allow higher QPS for embeddings but strict rates for generation?
[00:01:44] Ravi: Yes. We have route-level policies. In the Console policy editor you can create a policy like: for /v1/generate set token-based quota 200k per day; for /v1/embedding set 5k per minute; and you can choose whether overages are throttled or queued.
[00:01:58] Priya: Throttled or queued meaning?
[00:02:00] Ravi: Throttled means we reject with a 429. Queued means we can buffer within a short window if the policy allows burst capacity. You can also define burst windows that use Dedicated spare capacity.
[00:02:12] Jorge: How do you handle spikes from one tenant? We need per-tenant isolation so a noisy neighbor can't consume GPU.
[00:02:18] Ravi: There are two layers - logical and physical. Logically, project keys and per-project quotas limit request count and token usage at the gateway. Physically, Dedicated customers can reserve GPU pools per-tenant or per-project, or you can enable strict throttling on Hosted to keep noisy tenants under a ceiling. For multi-tenant workloads we usually recommend a hybrid: use Hosted with strict per-project quotas for early stages, then move to Dedicated and allocate pools when you need guaranteed throughput.
[00:02:45] Maya: And we have automatic fallback routes - if your preferred model is out of capacity we can route to a compatible quantized variant to keep requests served, with a flag in the Console to control that behavior.
[00:02:57] [00:03:22] Laura: Ok, what about billing and chargeback? We want to bill tenants based on token usage, but also apply a minimum subscription. Does Redwood expose token-level export?
[00:03:32] Ravi: Yes token-level breakdowns per request, and you can export per-key usage via CSV or our usage API. In the Console under Billing -> Usage you can filter by project or key and set up billing exports to S3 or to a web hook.
[00:03:50] Tom: Are the counters eventually consistent? Like if we read usage in real time for billing, how accurate is it?
[00:03:56] Ravi: We use eventual aggregation, usually under a minute lag for high-throughput. For precise billing we'll recommend using the billing export once per day and doing reconciliation, but for near real-time SOC dashboards the Console is very close.
[00:04:10] [00:04:40] Priya: Security questions - where are keys stored, how are they rotated, and what's the KMS story?
[00:04:46] Maya: Keys are stored encrypted at rest. For Private/Dedicated customers we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping. You can rotate keys in the Console, and we support key rotation with grace periods so existing sessions continue for a configurable window.
[00:05:01] Priya: Do you log the raw input for model requests? We have PHI concerns.
[00:05:05] Ravi: By default Hosted retains request/response logs for 30 days for debugging but you can disable retention or enable redaction. For HIPAA-regulated workloads we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC and no retention; we also provide options to redact PII at the gateway. We'll send the detailed security pack with these options.
[00:05:22] [00:05:50] Jorge: Can policies be applied by tag? We have tenants grouped by region and feature flags.
[00:05:56] Ravi: Yes you can tag projects and write policy rules that target tags - e.g., all projects with tag:eu get EU data residency handling and quotas tuned differently.
[00:06:06] Laura: Show us how to create a policy.
[00:06:09] [00:06:40] Ravi: (navigates) Policy editor. We'll create a new policy called "tenant-default-quota". Condition: request.project.tag != "internal". Actions: limit tokens to 150k/day, rate 30 requests/min, set response on overage to 429. Save. Now attach to all projects under the org or select specific projects - attaching produces an effective policy table.
[00:07:05] Tom: If we attach and then later change, is it immediate?
[00:07:08] Ravi: Policy changes are pushed near real-time at the gateway, usually under 10 seconds to propagate. There's a change history and you can schedule rollouts.
[00:07:18] [00:07:50] Laura: What about quotas for monthly committed usage vs burst? We want committed baseline for cost predictability but allow short bursts for growth.
[00:07:58] Maya: For Dedicated you can set reserved baseline capacity and configure a burst bucket that draws from a shared spare pool or from a paid burst rate. For Hosted you can reserve a committed tier which gives you predictable per-token pricing and a separate burst allowance for traffic spikes. We'll show pricing options in the follow-up.
[00:08:20] [00:08:55] Jorge: API detail: are rate limits enforced at API key granularity, IP, or account?
[00:09:01] Ravi: Primarily at API key/project granularity. You can also apply org-level soft-throttles. For IP-level controls we can integrate with WAF at the edge or you can set route-based IP allow/deny lists.
[00:09:12] Priya: Does the audit log capture policy changes and who made them?
[00:09:16] Ravi: Yes change events include user, timestamp, and before/after; logs are exportable to SIEMs like Splunk.
[00:09:23] [00:09:58] Laura: Can we demo the API shape for setting quotas programmatically?
[00:10:05] Ravi: Sure. (shares code) Example: POST /v1/policies with JSON body setting scope project_id and limits. The response returns a policy_id. You can also create policies via Terraform provider or our CLI. Note: the Console is just a wrapper; everything is available through API/infra-as-code.
[00:10:30] Tom: CLI or Terraform would be best for infra teams.
[00:10:33] Ravi: Yep we have a Terraform provider with resources for projects, keys, and policies.
[00:10:40] [00:11:28] Laura: Regarding org/project keys: can we rotate keys automatically every X days?
[00:11:33] Ravi: You can set rotation policies - automatic rotation window and notify stakeholders. For server keys we recommend rotation every 90 days, mobile keys should be scoped and short-lived.
[00:11:45] Priya: Is there support for short-lived tokens via your auth service?
[00:11:49] Maya: Yes we support JWT-based short-lived tokens minted by your auth system and presented to Redwood; the gateway validates the token and maps it to a project.
[00:11:59] [00:12:30] Jorge: Can you show how a noisy tenant would be throttled?
[00:12:34] Ravi: (switches demo) Here's a synthetic traffic sim. Project A is set to 30 rps and token cap 150k/day. I'm now firing a burst of 200 rps. You can see in real time the proxy returning 429s for requests beyond the rate and the Console alerts kicking in - an email and Slack webhook.
[00:12:56] Laura: Do alerts come with context - like top endpoints and sample request ids?
[00:13:00] Ravi: Alerts include aggregated metrics and you can link to a sample request trace. For privacy we truncate payloads unless logging is enabled.
[00:13:10] [00:13:45] Tom: If we need to temporarily raise a limit for a tenant, can we do that without redeploy?
[00:13:48] Ravi: Yes, you can edit the policy in Console or call the policies API and the change is effective immediately. We also support scheduled policy changes.
[00:14:02] Priya: For compliance we need proof of who changed a policy and when. The audit trail must be immutable.
[00:14:08] Ravi: Audit logs are immutable write-once and we can push them to a customer S3 bucket or SIEM. For high-assurance customers we support Signed Audit Logs and HSM-backed log signing.
[00:14:25] [00:14:53] Laura: What about rate limits by model family? If we have a cheaper quantized variant, can we force non-critical traffic to the cheaper model?
[00:15:00] Ravi: Yes, routing policies can be based on model family, cost threshold, and latency SLO. You can define rules: route high priority traffic to gpt-redwood-1, send low-priority to gpt-redwood-1-quant or open-source variants.
[00:15:15] Maya: This is part of Redwood Optimize - cost/performance toolkit suggests quantization profiles and routing policies based on your workload. We'll include a report in the follow-up.
[00:15:30] [00:16:12] Jorge: Let's talk pilot. We want to run a benchmark that mimics our traffic: 10 tenants at 5qps steady, with one tenant spiking to 50qps for 2 min. We need metrics on p95 latency, error rates, and cost per 1k tokens. Can Redwood run that?
[00:16:26] Maya: Yes we can run an internal benchmark or you can run it in your environment hitting our Hosted endpoints. For Dedicated we can spin up a pilot cluster. We'll do p95, p99, throughput, and cost projection.
[00:16:36] Tom: Network wise, for Dedicated we need VPC peering - is that supported?
[00:16:40] Ravi: Supported. We offer VPC peering and Private deployments with on-prem options. We'll include network diagrams in the security pack.
[00:16:53] [00:17:20] Priya: About data residency: some tenants are EU-only, can we restrict processing to certain regions?
[00:17:26] Ravi: Yes, you can tag projects and constrain them to run in a specific region. For stricter compliance we recommend Private deployments in your region or Dedicated capacity in our EU region.
[00:17:40] Laura: Could you show the billing export again?
[00:17:45] Ravi: Billing -> Exports. Choose frequency, project filter and destination S3. The CSV includes columns: timestamp, project_id, key_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, model, route.
[00:18:02] [00:18:35] Jorge: Any rate limits on the usage API itself?
[00:18:38] Ravi: Usage API is rate-limited but with high quotas for enterprise customers; we can allowped higher throughput for your reporting service.
[00:18:47] Maya: Quick note on quotas vs billing: you can set hard quotas that prevent usage (enforced) or soft quotas that alert but continue, which is useful for monitoring before you hit hard limits.
[00:19:05] [00:19:40] Laura: Are there built-in tenant-level dashboards? We'd like to give product managers a per-tenant view.
[00:19:46] Ravi: Yes per-project dashboards showing tokens, latency percentiles, error rates, and top prompts. Dashboards can be shared with read-only links or via SSO role-based access.
[00:19:58] Tom: How does RBAC map to org vs project admin?
[00:20:02] Ravi: Roles: Org Admin, Billing Admin, Project Admin, Project Viewer, and custom roles. Project Admins can manage keys and policies scoped to the project; Org Admins manage global policies and billing.
[00:20:12] [00:20:40] Priya: SSO integration - SAML or OIDC?
[00:20:44] Maya: Both. You can map SAML groups to Redwood roles and set MFA requirements.
[00:20:52] [00:21:20] Laura: In the Console I saw a "simulate policy" button earlier, what's that?
[00:21:24] Ravi: Simulate lets you run a hypothetical request against current policies and see whether it would be allowed, throttled, or routed to a fallback. It's useful for testing rules before applying.
[00:21:36] [00:22:10] Jorge: Are you able to show logs for a single request id?
[00:22:14] Ravi: Yes click a trace, you'll see timeline: request ingress, policy eval, routing decision, model call, and response. We show sampled request metadata; payloads are redacted unless enabled.
[00:22:30] [00:23:00] Tom: We want to auto-scale projects based on queue depth. Does Redwood support autoscaling policies per project?
[00:23:06] Ravi: For Dedicated yes - autoscaling policies can be per pool or per project allocation. You can trigger scale based on queue length, token backlog, or latency. For Hosted we do autoscaling at our infra layer but you can configure throttles and burst buckets.
[00:23:26] Maya: Also note, caching: prefix caching and KV cache help reduce calls for repeated prompts. That lowers cost and reduces load.
[00:23:38] [00:24:05] Laura: Any gotchas for multi-tenant log retention in terms of compliance?
[00:24:10] Priya: (interrupting) Specifically we need ability to purge a tenant's logs on request.
[00:24:14] Ravi: You can configure per-project retention and on-demand purge; for Hosted customers we recommend the Private option if you need guaranteed right-to-be-forgotten semantics. We'll document the purge APIs.
[00:24:30] [00:25:00] Laura: What's the SLA for rate limiting enforcement?
[00:25:04] Ravi: Enforcement is at the gateway and is highly available. For Dedicated we offer SLA on availability and p99 latency tiers per contract.
[00:25:16] [00:25:40] Maya: Wrapping up the demo portion - we've shown project keys, policy editor, alerts, audit logs, billing exports, and routing. Any specific concerns we haven't covered?
[00:25:50] Jorge: One last: can you do per-tenant model pinning? Some tenants must use enterprise model only.
[00:25:56] Ravi: Yes per-project model pinning is available. You can restrict a project to a model list; requests for disallowed models are rejected.
[00:26:07] [00:26:40] Laura: That covers most. Next steps?
[00:26:43] Maya: We'll send pricing and the security pack. Ravi will share the SOC2 and network diagrams. We propose a pilot week starting 2026-10-28 to run your benchmark.
[00:26:56] Tom: Sounds good. For the pilot environment do you need anything from our infra team?
[00:27:01] Ravi: Just network details if you want VPC peering and sample prompt sets. We'll provide instructions for hitting Hosted endpoints as well.
[00:27:10] Priya: Please also include the redaction and purge APIs in the pack.
[00:27:14] Maya: Will do.
[00:27:20] [00:27:50] Laura: One minor nit - we've had bad experiences where per-route policies didn't consider tokenization differences across models. How do you account for that?
[00:27:59] Ravi: Good question. Our token accounting normalizes to the model used for the request; when routing to a cheaper variant we re-evaluate expected token counts and annotate the usage record. The Optimize toolkit can simulate cost per model to avoid surprises.
[00:28:20] [00:28:55] Jorge: Can you provide an example policy JSON we can apply via API?
[00:28:59] Ravi: I'll include a sample in the follow-up - small snippet, policy scope: project_id, limits: {tokens_per_day:150000, requests_per_minute:30}, action: reject.
[00:29:12] [00:29:40] Maya: Alright, we'll move to questions from the team.
[00:29:45] Tom: For the billing export, can we map tokens to internal SKUs?
[00:29:50] Ravi: Yes you can enrich exports with tags and tags can map to product SKUs in your billing pipeline.
[00:29:58] [00:30:30] Priya: One more security check - for Dedicated, can we use our own HSM for log signing?
[00:30:36] Ravi: Yes HSM-backed signing and KMS integration are supported in Dedicated/Private. We'll send the integration doc.
[00:30:50] [00:31:20] Laura: Any limitation on number of project keys?
[00:31:24] Ravi: Practically no hard limit, we recommend grouping keys sensibly; we can increase quotas if needed.
[00:31:35] [00:32:05] Jorge: If we implement scheduled policy updates, is there a rollback?
[00:32:09] Ravi: Yes every policy change is versioned - you can rollback to previous versions easily and schedule rollbacks too.
[00:32:20] [00:33:00] Maya: OK final recap: 1) We'll send pricing and security pack, 2) Ravi shares SOC2 + network diagrams + sample policy JSON, 3) Hillcrest to provide sample prompt set and tenant list, 4) schedule pilot week starting 2026-10-28. Any objections?
[00:33:18] Laura: None.
[00:33:20] Jorge: Go ahead.
[00:33:22] Priya: Sounds fine.
[00:33:30] [00:34:05] Maya: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the docs and proposed pilot plan.
[00:34:12] Tom: Thanks.
[00:34:15] (meeting wraps; small chatter)
[00:34:40] End of recording.

Notes: transcript contains occasional auto-transcription artifacts, speaker overlap, and shorthand. Refer to follow-up materials for exact policy JSON and security docs.
